ai.description: *Gekko vittatus* reaches 25 cm. It is grey-brown with a distinctive white or yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral bands. It features adhesive toe pads and a prehensile tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gekko vittatus* is distinguished by a distinctive, unbroken creamy-white vertebral stripe running from the snout to the tail, a feature absent in other Indian *Gekko* species.
ai.habitat: The Sago Gecko is not native to the Indian subcontinent; it inhabits lowland tropical rainforests and coconut plantations in New Guinea and surrounding islands.
ai.behavior: The Sago gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects while utilizing its specialized toe pads to navigate vertical surfaces with remarkable agility.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gekko vittatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, though specific data for Indian populations is sparse.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gekko vittatus* is not native to the Indian subcontinent; it is endemic to Indonesia, New Guinea, and surrounding islands in the Indo-Pacific region.
